title: Release Candidate 0.4.0
description: to close https://github.com/r-lib/sparsevctrs/issues/163

title: Reject non-finite `default` in `sparse_double()`
description: `sparse_double()` accepted `Inf`, `-Inf` and `NaN` as `default`, which made `sum()` return `NaN` because it multiplied the default by zero stored positions. It now gives an error, consistent with `values`, which already rejects non-finite entries.

title: Support logical sparse matrices in `coerce_to_sparse_data_frame()`
description: `coerce_to_sparse_data_frame()` and `coerce_to_sparse_tibble()` failed with an error about `REAL()` for logical sparse matrices, which also broke the round trip from `coerce_to_sparse_matrix()` on empty integer data frames. The logical values are now turned into doubles, giving sparse double columns.

title: Fix `NaN` and integer `val` handling in scalar arithmetic functions
description: The scalar arithmetic functions treated `val = NaN` as `NA`, left stored values equal to the new default after underflow or rounding, and errored for a non-whole `val` on sparse integers only when a result happened to be fractional. They now return `NaN`, drop values equal to the new default, and always error for a non-whole `val` on sparse integers. Results that sparse doubles can't store, such as `Inf`, still give an error.

title: Warn and return `Inf` in `min()` and `max()` when no non-missing values remain
description: `min()` and `max()` on a sparse integer vector with `na.rm = TRUE` and nothing left returned `.Machine$integer.max` and `NA` instead of `Inf` and `-Inf`. They now return `Inf` and `-Inf` with a warning, as dense vectors do, and sparse double vectors give the same warning.

title: Match `var()` for dense and short input in `sparse_var()` and friends
description: `sparse_var()` and `sparse_sd()` returned `NA` for non-sparse input, which the design docs say the `sparse_*` helpers should support. They now work for dense input and return `NA` when fewer than 2 non-missing observations remain, like `var()`. `sparse_mean()` and `sparse_median()` of a length-0 vector now return `NaN` and `NA` instead of the default, also matching base R.

title: Fix integer overflow and zero-sum weights in `sparse_mean()`
description: `sparse_mean()` overflowed on sparse integer vectors with a large length and default, which also made `sparse_var()` and `sparse_sd()` return `NA`. With weights that sum to zero it also returned the default instead of `NaN` like `weighted.mean()`. The NA-weight behavior with `na_rm = TRUE` is unchanged and now documented.

title: Reject `NaN` and `Inf` in sparse matrices in `coerce_to_sparse_data_frame()`
description: Sparse matrices containing `NaN` or `Inf` skipped the validation that data frames get, so the resulting sparse columns gave wrong `min()` and `max()` results. `coerce_to_sparse_data_frame()` and `coerce_to_sparse_tibble()` now error on these values for matrix input, matching the data frame path.

title: Fix `sum()` overflowing silently on sparse integer vectors
description: `sum()` on a sparse integer vector accumulated into an `int`, so sums outside the integer range wrapped around without any signal. It now accumulates in 64 bits and returns a double when the result doesn't fit in an integer, matching what `sum()` does for dense integer vectors in current R versions.

title: Keep missing values in `sparse_dummy()` for a single-level factor
description: `sparse_dummy(one_hot = TRUE)` on a single-level factor returned 1 for missing elements, contradicting the documented behavior that a missing value gives missing values in every dummy variable. The single-level shortcut is now only taken when `x` has no missing values, so factors with NA go through the regular path.

title: Keep stored `Inf` and `NaN` times 0 in `sparse_multiplication()` results
description:
Stacked on #152, so the base is that branch and it will retarget to `main` once #152 merges.

A stored `Inf` or `NaN` in a sparse double vector multiplied by 0 was dropped (`Inf`) or returned as `NA` (`NaN`), where dense R gives `NaN`. Stored non-finite values only come from in-place modification or the matrix path.

```r
x <- sparse_double(c(2, 3), c(1, 2), 4)
x[3] <- Inf
sparse_multiplication(x, c(0, 0, 0, 0))
#> before: 0 0 0 0
#> after:  0 0 NaN 0
sparse_multiplication_scalar(x, 0)
#> before: 0 0 0 0
#> after:  0 0 NaN 0
```

This applies to the sparse-dense and sparse-sparse paths of `sparse_multiplication()` and to the `val = 0` branch of `sparse_multiplication_scalar()`. The result stores the `NaN` instead of erroring or going dense, which matches #152. The scalar docs now mention this exception. Integer vectors are unchanged.

`is_na_at()` and `poke_na()` were unused after this and are removed. Three new tests cover the cases above.

title: Keep `0 * Inf` and `0 * NaN` in `sparse_multiplication()` dense operands
description:
`sparse_multiplication()` dropped positions where a sparse vector has its default value of 0 and the dense operand has `Inf`, `-Inf` or `NaN`, because only `NA` got an explicit entry. Dense R gives `NaN` there (`0 * Inf`).

```r
x <- sparse_double(c(2, 3), c(1, 2), 4)
sparse_multiplication(x, c(1, 1, Inf, NaN))
#> before: 2 3 0 0
#> after:  2 3 NaN NaN
```

`multiplication_sparse_dense()` now finds every non-finite dense value outside the stored positions and writes `0 * y` there (an explicit `NA` stays `NA`). Both argument orders and an empty sparse operand are covered, and integer behavior is unchanged.

Tests cover non-finite values at default positions in both orders, an empty sparse operand, non-finite values at stored positions, and a stored `NA` mixed with `Inf`. Seven of the new expectations fail on the old code.

A stored `Inf`/`NaN` on the sparse side is handled in a follow-up PR.

title: Return NA with a warning when sparse_multiplication() overflows integers
description: Integer products in `sparse_multiplication()` were computed with a plain `int` multiply, which is undefined behavior on overflow and wrapped silently (`100000L * 100000L` gave `1410065408`). They now give `NA` with the `NAs produced by integer overflow` warning, as dense integer vectors do, which also fixes `sparse_mean()` with integer weights.

title: Add tests for `sparse_multiplication()` with non-sparse ALTREP inputs
description: Follow-up to #148, which fixed \`sparse_multiplication()\` erroring on non-sparsevctrs ALTREP inputs such as \`sort()\` output. This adds regression tests for that case and drops the R-side check that the C dispatch made redundant.

title: Fix sparse methods returning stale results after in-place modification
description:
After \`x[i] <- value\`, methods like \`sum()\`, \`max()\`, \`anyNA()\`, \`x[i]\` and \`sparse_values()\` kept answering from the original stored values and gave results that disagreed with the dense vector. They now rebuild the stored values and positions from the materialized data first, so results match dense R while sparse subsetting is preserved.

\`sparse_multiplication()\` also now dispatches only on sparsevctrs vectors, so other ALTREP inputs such as \`sort()\` output take the dense path.

title: Rewrite the scalar arithmetic functions in C
description:
The four scalar arithmetic functions (`sparse_addition_scalar()`, `sparse_subtraction_scalar()`, `sparse_multiplication_scalar()` and `sparse_division_scalar()`) now do their work in C instead of building a new sparse vector from R vectors. The R wrappers keep the cheap shortcuts (`NA`, identity values, the dense `val = 0` division result from #146) and then call one shared C routine with an operation tag.

On this machine a call on a small sparse vector goes from about 10 us to about 1.5 us. With one million stored doubles, addition goes from 9.8 ms to 2.6 ms, multiplication from 6.2 ms to 3.4 ms and division from 6.2 ms to 3.0 ms. Integer vectors improve less, 6.2 ms to 4.6 ms for addition.

I compared the old and new code over a grid of 1368 inputs and values, and every case where the old code succeeded gives the same result. The intended differences, all noted in `NEWS.md`:

* Stored integer values that overflow now give `NA` with the usual "NAs produced by integer overflow" warning, as dense integer vectors do, instead of an error. An overflowing default value still errors.
* `sparse_division_scalar()` now errors for sparse logical input, instead of silently accepting it.
* Results that sparse double vectors can't store (stored `Inf` or `NaN`, or a `NaN` default) still error, with clearer messages.
* A result that happens to equal the default value no longer errors.
* A fractional `val` still works on sparse integer vectors when every result is a whole number, and errors otherwise.

Multiplying by 0 keeps stored `NA` values in C too, so the fix from #145 is not undone. The test added there fails against the earlier version of this C code.

Closes #88.

title: Make `sparse_division_scalar()` match dense division when val is 0
description:
`sparse_division_scalar(x, 0)` returned `Inf` at every position, whatever the values of `x` were. Dense R gives `-Inf` for negative values, `NaN` for zeros and `NA` for missing values, so the sparse result did not match `x[] / 0`. The existing test asserted the `Inf` result, which only held because that input happened to be non-negative where it mattered.

Sparse vectors can't store `Inf`, `-Inf` or `NaN`, so the result is still a regular double vector, as before. It is now built from the default and the stored values separately, so it matches dense division for sparse integer and double vectors with any default, and the input is not materialized. The docs now say that a dense vector is returned when `val = 0`.

The two assertions in the existing division test are updated to compare against dense division, and there is a new test covering negative values, stored `NA`s, non-zero defaults, empty vectors and zero-length vectors.

Follow up to #145. Related to #88.

title: Keep stored `NA` values in `sparse_multiplication_scalar()` when val is 0
description:
`sparse_multiplication_scalar(x, 0)` returned a vector with no stored values, which silently dropped any stored `NA`. Dense R gives `NA * 0 = NA`, so the sparse result did not match `x[] * 0`.

When `val` is 0, the result now keeps the positions of the stored `NA` values and drops everything else (non-`NA` values become 0, which equals the default). This applies to both sparse integer and sparse double vectors, with zero and non-zero defaults.

This is split out from the C rewrite of the scalar arithmetic functions so the behavior change is reviewed on its own. Related to #88.

title: Speed up `sparse_dummy()`
description:
Speeds up `sparse_dummy()`, closing #81. The level counts now come from a single pass in C instead of several passes in R, each level's data pointer is cached instead of looked up for every row, and missing values are written one level at a time instead of being scattered across every level for each missing row.

On an optimized build (Apple silicon) it is 36 to 95% faster than `main` in every case I benchmarked, for example 1e6 rows with 1000 levels and 5% missing values drops from about 620 ms to 34 ms. Few levels with many missing values gains the least (1e6 rows, 10 levels, 5% missing: 8.6 ms to 4.0 ms). The output is unchanged.

title: Let coerce_to_sparse_data_frame() take data frames and tibbles
description:
`coerce_to_sparse_data_frame()` now also accepts a data frame or tibble and turns each integer, double, logical, or character column into a sparse vector of the same type, keeping column and row names. Columns of any other type (factors, dates, and so on) give an error naming the columns and their types, in line with `coerce_to_sparse_matrix()` rejecting non-numeric columns.

Closes #126.

title: Share typed `Materialize`, `Extract_subset` and `Min`/`Max` ALTREP helpers
description:
Closes #134.

Adds `static inline` typed helpers to `altrep-sparse-common.h` for `Materialize` and `Extract_subset` (`sparse_int_*`, `sparse_dbl_*`, `sparse_chr_*`; logical reuses the `int` helpers), and collapses `Min` and `Max` into one helper per file for the integer and double types. No X-macros, as planned in the issue. Behavior is unchanged: the full test suite passes with no snapshot changes.

## Line counts

The diff is +242 and -195, so net +47 lines. The four ALTREP `.c` files are about 140 lines shorter, but the typed helpers in the header add 145 lines because each type keeps its own copy of the loop. This removes duplicated logic across files rather than shrinking the total.

## Timings

Length 1e7, 1e5 stored values, median of 30 runs, measured before and after on the same machine. `Extract_subset` subsets with 1e6 indices.

| Case           | Before (ms) | After (ms) |
| -------------- | ----------- | ---------- |
| Materialize    | 22.5        | 24         |
| Extract_subset | 68          | 68         |
| min            | 2           | 2          |

No regression, so no helper was reverted.

## Left as is

`Elt`, `Sum` and the double `Is_sorted` stay per type. Their bodies differ in overflow handling, NA checks and accessors, so sharing them would need branches or per-element function pointers, which is no clearer and risks slowing the per-element `Elt` callback.

title: Fix doc typos and scalar arithmetic defaults, and add edge case tests
description: Fixes the remaining doc typos and keeps the old `sparse-arithmatic` topic names and reference URLs working. Adding edge case tests turned up that `sparse_multiplication_scalar()` and `sparse_division_scalar()` never scaled the default value, so vectors with a non-zero default gave wrong results. That is fixed here too.

title: Sort the output of `sparse_multiplication()` in O(n log n) time
description: The sort of the result in `sparse_multiplication()` was a bubble sort, so sparse by dense with 1e6 stored values took about 84 s and sparse by sparse with 1e6 stored values on each side did not finish in over 10 minutes. It is now a merge sort on an index, taking 0.03 s and 0.015 s for those cases.

title: Share the integer and double code in `sparse_multiplication()`
description:
The integer and double versions of sparse-by-sparse, sparse-by-dense and dense-by-dense multiplication now share one implementation each, which removes about 200 lines. Timings on an optimized build are unchanged.

Sharing the code also fixes sparse double by dense multiplication returning duplicated positions when a stored `NA` met a fractional dense value, because the old code truncated the dense value to an integer.

title: Share the sparse ALTREP helpers between the vector types
description: The four sparse ALTREP files repeated the same constructor, `Dataptr_or_null`, `Inspect`, `Duplicate`, `Elt` lookup and `Extract_subset` matching code, so those now live in `altrep-sparse-common.{c,h}`. Integer and logical also share `Is_sorted` and `No_NA`. `Min`, `Max`, `Sum` and `Materialize` are left per type, because their accumulator and return types differ. There is no user-facing change, and an optimized build showed no timing change in subsetting, materializing, `Elt`, `sum()`, `min()` or multiplication.

title: Fix sparse `Elt` bounds and `sparse_multiplication()` with no stored values
description: Fixes the off-by-one bounds check in the sparse `Elt` methods, adds a checked length conversion in `sparse_dummy()`, and fixes `sparse_multiplication()` erroring when one sparse input has no stored values. A read-only protection review of the C code found nothing to change.

title: Fix scalar arithmetic errors and `sparse_replace_na()` for logicals
description: Scalar arithmetic on sparse logical or character vectors now gives a clear error instead of an object not found error, and `sparse_replace_na()` now handles sparse logical vectors. The `sparse_multiplication()` error messages are also fixed (typo, wrong variable reported), with a snapshot test for each.

title: Move the C code to the rlang C library
description:
Vendors the rlang C library and moves all of the package's C code onto it (`r_obj*`, `r_ssize`, `KEEP()`/`FREE()`, pointer based loops), following the layout and naming conventions of vctrs and rlang: `ffi_` wrappers first in each file, decl headers, `static` helpers, and a shared `sparsevctrs-core.h`. Behavior is unchanged apart from two latent fixes found while reading for protection: a list left unprotected in `sparse-dummy.c` and `nas` left unprotected in the sparse-sparse multiplication, plus the logical `NA` check in `altrep-sparse-logical.c`, which never matched before.

`arithmatic` is renamed to `arithmetic`, and the conventions are documented in `.claude/CLAUDE.md`. Sharing code between the four ALTREP types is left for #134.

title: Fix sparse is.unsorted() for numeric and logical vectors
description: Sparse integer, double, and logical `is.unsorted()` ignored default values after the last stored value, and treated a vector with a single stored value as sorted without comparing it to the default. For example, `is.unsorted(sparse_double(5, 1, 10))` returned `FALSE` for `5, 0, 0, ...`. This brings them in line with the sparse character fix.

title: Fix sparse min() and max() when every position is stored
description: Sparse integer and double `min()` and `max()` always counted the default value, even when every position held an explicit value and the default was not in the vector. For example, `min(sparse_double(c(5, 6), 1:2, 2))` returned 0 instead of 5. The default is now only considered when at least one position is unstored.

title: Fix sparse logical sum and sparse string Is_sorted
description: Fixes a wrong default extractor in sparse logical `sum()`, and several bugs in the sparse character `Is_sorted` method: a leftover debug print, comparison of string pointers instead of contents, and default values after the last stored value being ignored.

title: Speed up coerce_to_sparse_data_frame()
description:
Closes #66.

On a 67,000 x 16,000 sparse matrix (0.1% density), `coerce_to_sparse_data_frame()` goes from about 450 ms to 11 ms, and `coerce_to_sparse_tibble()` from about 450 ms to 25 ms.

* Columns are built without per-column validation, since a `dgCMatrix` already guarantees sorted, unique, in-range positions.
* The per-column loop is now a C function (`ffi_sparse_matrix_to_list()`).
* The data frame is built directly instead of through `as.data.frame()`. Column names still go through `make.names(unique = TRUE)` so they match the old behavior.
* Explicit stored zeros are dropped up front with `Matrix::drop0()`, so they still can't end up equal to the default.

The two commits are separable: the first is R-only and gets most of the gain (about 26 ms), the second adds the C loop for the rest.

title: Add "Supported By Posit" badge to sparsevctrs website
description:
## Overview

This PR adds the "Supported by Posit" badge to the sparsevctrs website.

## Background

We've recently started adding a "Supported by Posit" badge across all Posit package websites to create a more cohesive brand presence. The badge appears on the far right of the top navigation bar or at the bottom of the hamburger menu. It links to Posit’s main website. @hadley is involved with this initiative.

The following websites already have the "Supported by Posit" badge: [ggplot2](https://ggplot2.tidyverse.org), [Great Tables](https://posit-dev.github.io/great-tables/articles/intro.html), [gt](https://gt.rstudio.com), [Plotnine](https://plotnine.org), [Pointblank](https://posit-dev.github.io/pointblank/), [pointblank](https://rstudio.github.io/pointblank/), and [Quarto](https://quarto.org).

See https://posit-dev.github.io/supported-by-posit/ for more information.

## Changes

- Added a line to `_pkgdown.yml` to include the JavaScript file
- Standardized indentation in `_pkgdown.yml`

## Screenshots

At 1200px browser width:

title: Sparse arithmatic scalar helper functions
description:
all the arithmetic operations are fairly simple for sparse vectors when done with a scalar. these functions help when we wanna preserve sparsity

``` r
library(sparsevctrs)

vec <- sparse_integer(5, 1, 100000)

is_sparse_vector(
  vec
)
#> [1] TRUE

is_sparse_vector(
  vec * 5
)
#> [1] FALSE

is_sparse_vector(
  sparse_multiplication_scalar(vec, 5) 
)
#> [1] TRUE
```

title: Add `has_sparse_elements()`
description:
To close #70 

We see good speedups for wide fully sparse tibbles, and even small speedup for worst case scenario of no sparsity.

``` r
library(sparsevctrs)

set.seed(1234)
n_cols <- 10000
mat <- matrix(sample(0:1, n_cols * 10, TRUE, c(0.9, 0.1)), ncol = n_cols)
colnames(mat) <- as.character(seq_len(n_cols))
sparse_mat <- Matrix::Matrix(mat, sparse = TRUE)

res <- coerce_to_sparse_tibble(sparse_mat)

old_version <- function(x) {
  any(vapply(x, is_sparse_vector, logical(1)))
}

bench::mark(
  old_version(res),
  has_sparse_elements(res)
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   expression                    min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr>               <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 old_version(res)           8.63ms    8.9ms      110.   46.46KB     41.5
#> 2 has_sparse_elements(res) 901.99ns   1.02µs   926799.    4.84KB      0

res <- as.data.frame(as.matrix(res))

bench::mark(
  old_version(res),
  has_sparse_elements(res)
)
#> # A tibble: 2 × 6
#>   expression                    min   median `itr/sec` mem_alloc `gc/sec`
#>   <bch:expr>               <bch:tm> <bch:tm>     <dbl> <bch:byt>    <dbl>
#> 1 old_version(res)           3.28ms   3.44ms      289.    39.1KB     25.9
#> 2 has_sparse_elements(res)   2.35ms   2.45ms      407.        0B     22.5
```
